title: IR Reflectance Threshold Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: See how surface color, distance, and the trimmer threshold decide whether an active-LOW IR sensor reads 0 (surface detected) or 1 (nothing detected).

educational.topic: IR reflectance sensors, thresholds, and active-LOW outputs
learningObjectives: Predict whether an active-LOW IR sensor reads 0 or 1 for a given surface and distance.
Set the trimmer threshold so the sensor switches at a chosen distance.
Choose a threshold that separates a black surface from a white surface.
prerequisites: GPIO input pins and HIGH/LOW logic (Chapter 6)

controls.label: White / Gray / Black
controls.purpose: Choose the surface under the sensor.

controls.label: Auto-calibrate
controls.purpose: Set the threshold halfway between the black and white readings at the current distance.

controls.label: Bright room
controls.purpose: Add 15 points of ambient IR to every reading, capped at 100.

controls.label: Distance
controls.purpose: Height of the sensor above the surface.

equations: peak = 1.0 (white), 0.55 (gray), 0.15 (black); ambient = 15 in a bright room, else 0
assumptions: The sensor output is active LOW.
Reflection falls off smoothly with distance.
limitations: Real modules have a minimum range and depend on surface texture and angle.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, then check against a graph with a live threshold
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter exploration with a marked switch point and a calibration button
keyQuestions: Why does a white surface make the sensor read 0?
Where does the output switch from 0 to 1, and how does the threshold move that point?
Why can a bright room make black and white look the same?
commonMisconceptions: An output of 1 means a surface was detected.
A black surface reflects more IR because it looks darker.
One threshold works in every room and at every height.
assessmentOpportunities: Find the largest distance where white still reads 0 at threshold 40.
Name a threshold that separates black from white at 4 cm.
Predict 0 or 1 for three given surface, distance, and threshold cases.
